bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42495373 (assimp): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target assimp_fuzzer [asan].
bug_description.normalized: The staged LightWave witness contains an overlong LoadObjectLayer path and blank LoadObject entries. LWS::Element::Parse copies those line tails into tokens[1]. For the crashing object, SetupNodeName formats the overlong path into aiNode::mName with ai_snprintf and stores the unclamped would-have-been length in aiString.length; BuildGraph then attempts to rename the same node to Pivot: + name, but aiString::Set(const std::string&) rejects the oversized replacement and preserves the bogus length. Separately, FindLWOFile turns an empty LoadObject filename into ../, X3DImporter::CanRead misclassifies that path via find_last_of(".x3d"), and X3DImporter returns a stub scene. The successful attachment makes MergeScenes reach AddNodePrefixesChecked, which passes the preserved oversized aiString.length to SuperFastHash and triggers the ASAN heap-buffer-overflow read past the 1144-byte aiNode allocated at LWSLoader.cpp:884.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the vulnerability-relevant input. The parser copies the remainder of each LWS line into tokens[1], creating both the overlong LoadObjectLayer path that later corrupts aiString metadata and blank LoadObject entries later converted to ../ by FindLWOFile.
source.value_from: Stage 02 rendered the staged poc as CR-delimited text and observed one 1205-byte LoadObjectLayer line, three standalone LoadObject lines with empty tails, and no literal '..' bytes; the saved sanitizer/default traces separately log one queued external file as ../ before the crash.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant taint is external-object path text parsed from LoadObjectLayer and LoadObject entries. The helper call at line 584 stores the overlong object path that later corrupts aiString.length, and the equivalent call at line 602 turns a blank LoadObject tail into ../ for the X3D misdispatch branch.

root_cause.description: SetupNodeName stores snprintf's would-have-been length directly into aiString.length without clamping it to the fixed aiString buffer size. For an overlong external-object path, aiString.data is truncated to 1023 bytes but aiString.length remains larger than the buffer, so later code trusts a bogus length.
root_cause.note: The registry patch resolves the witness only indirectly by disabling X3DImporter by default, which keeps MergeScenes on its empty-attachment fast path. It does not clamp the line-323 length corruption that step 4 later preserves on the crashing aiNode.

sink.description: ASAN crash site. SuperFastHash trusts the oversized aiString.length passed from AddNodePrefixesChecked and performs 16-bit reads past the end of the aiNode allocation that contains the truncated name buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports READ of size 1 at 0x61900000b3f9, one byte to the right of the 1144-byte region [0x61900000af80,0x61900000b3f8) allocated for the aiNode at LWSLoader.cpp:884.

parser_admitted.description: The witness is accepted as a LightWave motion/scene file because the first parsed token is LWMO, so the importer stays on the LWS path that later builds external-object requests and merges attached scenes.

coarse_trace.summary: The LWS parser copies attacker-controlled line tails into tokens[1], preserving both an overlong LoadObjectLayer path and blank LoadObject entries with empty filenames.

BuildGraph formats the overlong external-object path into an aiString, stores snprintf's unclamped would-have-been length, and then fails to apply the later Pivot rename because aiString::Set(std::string) early-returns on the oversized replacement.
A blank LoadObject entry is converted into ../, queued, and later misclassified as X3D, so the experimental importer returns a dummy aiScene instead of failing.
The successful ../ import makes attach nonempty, so the final MergeScenes call stays off the empty-attachment fast path and proceeds into unique-name handling.
AddNodePrefixesChecked hashes the preserved corrupt master node name, and SuperFastHash reads past the aiNode allocation, triggering the ASAN heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Element::Parse copies each line tail into tokens[1]. In the staged poc this materializes both the 1205-byte LoadObjectLayer tail that later corrupts aiString metadata and repeated bare LoadObject lines whose empty tails later resolve to ../.

The LoadObjectLayer handler stores the attacker-controlled external path in d.path for the object node later named by SetupNodeName. For the 1205-byte witness line, that basename plus the _(%08X) suffix exceeds aiString::MAXLEN - 1.

SetupNodeName writes the basename into nd->mName.data with ai_snprintf but stores the would-have-been length directly in nd->mName.length. On the top-level aiNode allocated at LWSLoader.cpp:884, the buffer is truncated to aiString's 1023-byte payload while length remains larger than the buffer.

BuildGraph then tries to rename the same aiNode to Pivot: + current name. aiString::operator=(const std::string&) calls aiString::Set(const std::string&) at include/assimp/types.h:297-304, and because the replacement string is still longer than MAXLEN - 1 the setter returns without changing the object, so the truncated buffer and oversized mName.length from step 3 are preserved.

A different rendered line is exactly LoadObject with an empty tail. In the LoadObject branch, after parsing the optional numeric id, c points to an empty string when FindLWOFile is invoked for that external request.

fine_trace.code: std::string test = std::string("..") + (io->getOsSeparator() + tmp); if (io->Exists(test)) { return test; }
fine_trace.note: With in == "", tmp stays empty, so the package-scene fallback constructs ../ on this non-Windows run and returns it when the parent directory exists. The saved vulnerable trace later logs this same resolved request as File: ../.
AddLoadRequest normalizes the resolved path into the batch queue: it creates or reuses a request id for file ../, so later loading sees a queued external file value of ../.
LoadAll dispatches the queued external request to importer selection. The saved run logs BEGIN EXTERNAL FILE, File: ../, and Load ../ at this point.

fine_trace.code: std::string::size_type pos = pFile.find_last_of(".x3d"); if (pos != std::string::npos) { return true; }
fine_trace.note: Importer selection reaches X3DImporter::CanRead for pFile = ../. find_last_of(".x3d") matches the '.' character in ../, so the experimental X3D importer incorrectly claims this non-X3D path.
The X3D stub returns a non-null aiScene for ../ by creating a root aiNode named after the path. This turns the misdispatch into a live external scene object instead of a load failure.

When BuildGraph revisits that external-object node, batch.GetImport(src.id) returns the imported ../ scene and the node is appended to attach. This successful attachment is what makes the later merge process additional scenes instead of copying only the master LWS graph.

This final merge call receives the nonempty attachment list from step 11. That bypasses MergeScenes's srcList.empty() fast path, and the call site includes the AI_INT_MERGE_SCENE_GEN_UNIQUE_NAMES_IF_NECESSARY flag that later routes node names through AddNodePrefixesChecked.

AddNodePrefixesChecked hashes each node name using the raw aiString.length field. For the master LWS object node from step 4, it pairs the truncated name buffer with the preserved oversized length and forwards both to SuperFastHash.

SuperFastHash trusts the oversized length from step 13 and keeps reading in 4-byte chunks until it crosses the 1144-byte aiNode allocation that contains the truncated name buffer. ASAN reports the resulting 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at 0x61900000b3f9, one byte past [0x61900000af80,0x61900000b3f8).

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: indirect: the unclamped aiString length is stored inside the same aiNode allocation later overread by SuperFastHash

format.name: LightWave scene/motion text with overlong LoadObjectLayer path and blank LoadObject entry resolving to ../
format.contract: The staged witness is a LightWave scene/motion file accepted by the LWS importer whose CR-delimited text includes one 1205-byte LoadObjectLayer line and at least one bare LoadObject line with an empty tail. The long LoadObjectLayer path must make the formatted object name exceed aiString::MAXLEN - 1, and the blank LoadObject line must make FindLWOFile resolve ../ in the saved run so the X3D stub returns a scene and merge-time hashing reaches the poisoned master node name.

patch_analysis.patch_description: The fix does not clamp aiString.length in SetupNodeName. Instead, ImporterRegistry only registers X3DImporter when ASSIMP_ENABLE_DEV_IMPORTERS is enabled, so the saved ../ request no longer yields a successful external scene during default runs. Without that scene, attach stays empty and MergeScenes returns before AddNodePrefixesChecked hashes the poisoned LWS node name.

key_changes.change: Adds ASSIMP_ENABLE_DEV_IMPORTERS environment gating and only pushes X3DImporter when the gate is enabled.
Removes X3DImporter from the default importer set, which prevents the saved ../ external request from producing a live aiScene and keeps SceneCombiner off the crashing path.

evidence_limitations: The staged witness contains three blank LoadObject lines. Because BatchLoader::AddLoadRequest deduplicates identical file/map pairs, the static artifacts prove that a blank LoadObject entry resolves to the single queued ../ request seen in the saved logs, but they do not distinguish which original blank line later first consumes that shared request id.
